prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on dev, and in a past world 12 varied trials all scored 0 in both training and dev. So I treat this as a regime where nothing learns yet, and I am not refining anything. Each candidate tests a different hypothesis:
(1) The default recipe gives only about 32 policy updates, so I try many smaller, more frequent updates.
(2) Extreme sample reuse with a long horizon.
(3) A uniform starting policy from zero-initialised outputs, with a separate value trunk and a learned DONE summary built from the observation.
(4) A flat output head that can learn any action layout, in case the stated interface is wrong.
(5) A per-type large-kernel convolution head with mask inputs, in case the anchor or orientation differs.
(6) A shared network applied to each layer that learns which layer a brick lands on through a softmax gate over layers.
Any non-zero training success should be confirmed in round 2.

### Round 2
Five of the six round-1 trials scored 0 in training and on dev. Only r1c5 scored above 0: training 0.0016, dev 0.002 (1 of 512 designs). On one seed that is barely more than nothing, but it is the only signal so far. r1c5 differs from the others in two ways. It feeds the legality mask in as per-type maps, and its per-type 5x5 output head can learn shifted or swapped footprints. Round 1 ruled out, at least for the starting network: few updates vs. many, 2 vs. 8 epochs, long horizon, uniform init, a separate value trunk and DONE summary, and per-layer depth bias. As in the past world, recipe and network family did not matter. Together with the note that this world may differ from its description, this points to a mismatch between the action layout and the observation layout. This round tests that with a head that sums over 32 possible action layouts (two variants), confirms r1c5 with more updates, isolates the effect of the mask input, and tries two r1c5 refinements.

### Round 3
Only one network family has learned: the per-type 5x5 conv output head with the legality mask fed in as maps (r1c5 dev 0.002, r2c3 dev 0.0645 with training success 0.042). The other networks all scored 0: the pooled head, even with the mask input (r2c5); both layout-mixture runs; the flat head; and the per-layer net. So the mask input alone does not explain the result, and the action layout is probably not the cause. The flexible 5x5 head seems to be the key ingredient, though this rests on single seeds. Going from 22 to 44 updates (r1c5 to r2c3) went with the jump in dev success. However, r2c6 also had many updates (about 83, with 2 epochs, lr 2e-3 and entropy 0.003) and scored 0, so the cause is confounded. This round keeps the r2c3 network and varies updates per sample, credit horizon, global context, a cheaper and deeper trunk that gets more samples, and learning rate. Each candidate makes one change.

### Round 4
The thing that matters most is the head. Only the per-type 5x5 conv head with mask-map inputs (r1c5 family) has learned. The other heads scored 0 or near 0: pooled, flat, layout-mixture, and the start arch with mask input added. Layout mismatch is ruled out. After that, more updates and more samples helped. Going from r1c5 to r2c3 to r3c1 (22, 44, 88 updates) raised dev from 0.002 to 0.065 to 0.117. The cheaper 32-wide, 4-conv trunk with 131k samples (r3c5) did best at 0.135. Some recipe changes hurt: 8-step rollouts (r3c2), gamma 0.99 (r3c3), and r2c6's mix of 2 epochs, lr 2e-3 and entropy 0.003. lr 2e-3 alone (r3c6) and global context (r3c4) were inside noise. Each of these is a single seed, so the differences of a few points are weak evidence. In this last round every candidate refines r3c5: more updates (64 or 96 envs), use of the unused compute (5 convs), more samples (3 epochs), and a deeper, narrower trunk.

## Trial it ended with
name: Narrow deep trunk (24x6)
hypothesis: A 24-wide trunk with 6 residual 3x3 convs costs about 0.7 of the starting network, so it keeps the full 131k samples. With the 5x5 head its receptive field covers the whole grid several times over. The deeper stack can build up multi-step features such as landing layers and sealed gaps. If dev falls clearly below 0.135, width matters more than depth at this budget.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
